meta.title: Rates of Reaction — Exam Review
meta.subject: Chemistry
meta.objective: Answer exam questions on rates of reaction and mark them accurately

questions.q: State one factor that increases the rate of a reaction.
questions.a: Increasing temperature (or concentration / surface area / a catalyst).

questions.q: Name the unit for rate of reaction when a gas is collected.

build.question: Explain how increasing the concentration of a reactant affects the rate of reaction. Refer to collision theory.
build.instruction: Mark each answer against the mark scheme. Give it a level and a mark out of 6.

levelDescriptors.desc: Detailed, coherent explanation linking concentration to collision frequency and to the rate.
Some linked points, but the explanation is incomplete.
Simple statements with no clear links.

indicativeContent.text: Increasing concentration means more particles in the same volume.
Collisions between particles happen more often.
So there are more successful collisions per second.
Therefore the rate of reaction increases.

doesNotAward: Particles move faster (that is the effect of temperature, not concentration).

samples.label: Student A
samples.text: When you add more concentration {x}the particles move faster{/x} so they {2}hit each other more{/2} and {4}the reaction speeds up.{/4}
misses: link to more particles in the same volume

samples.label: Student B
samples.text: More concentration means there are {1}more particles in the same volume,{/1} so {2}collisions happen more often.{/2} This gives {3}more successful collisions per second,{/3} so {4}the rate of reaction increases.{/4}
hits: more particles in the same volume
samples.comment: Clear, fully linked chain of reasoning.

samples.label: Student C
samples.text: {4}The rate goes up{/4} because {x}the particles have more energy{/x} when you add more of the reactant.
samples.comment: States the outcome but the reason is a misconception (energy, not frequency).

rows.q: Q1(a) Name the unit of rate

build.modelAnswer: {1}Concrete.{/1} The heater was on for the {2}longest time{/2}, so it was supplied with the most energy.

developing.q: Describe what happens to the rate of reaction as temperature increases.
developing.a: The rate increases: particles move faster, collide more often, and more collisions have enough energy to react.

reaching.q: A reaction produces 48 cm^3 of gas in 60 s. Calculate the mean rate of reaction.

mastering.q: Explain how increasing the concentration of a reactant affects the rate of reaction. Refer to collision theory in your answer.

levelDescriptors.desc: Detailed, coherent explanation linking concentration to collision frequency and to the rate.
Some linked points, but the explanation is incomplete.
Simple statements with no clear links.

indicativeContent.text: Increasing concentration means more particles in the same volume.
The particles are closer together / more crowded.
Collisions between particles happen more often.
So there are more collisions per second.
This gives more successful collisions per second.
Therefore the rate of reaction increases.

doesNotAward: Particles move faster (that is the effect of temperature, not concentration).

developing.q: Describe what happens to the rate of reaction as temperature increases.
developing.a: Rate increases — more frequent and more energetic collisions.

reaching.q: A reaction produces 48 cm^3 of gas in 60 s. Calculate the mean rate.

mastering.q: Explain how concentration affects rate using collision theory.
mastering.a: More particles per unit volume, so more frequent collisions and more successful collisions per second, so the rate increases.

questions.q: Explain why powdered marble reacts faster with acid than marble chips.
questions.a: Powder has a larger surface area so there are more frequent collisions between acid particles and marble particles.
